CPRI (Central Power Research Institute) Testing Scope & Submission:
Central Power Research Institute (CPRI), Sir C.V. Raman Road, Sadashivanagar, P.B. No. 8066, Bengaluru 560080 (and regional units in Bhopal, Hyderabad, Nagpur, Noida, Kolkata).
Disciplines & Testing Scope: Short-circuit testing, high-voltage transformers (IS 1180), switchgear & controlgear, lightning arresters, electric vehicle (EV) supply equipment & chargers, power cables, and smart meters.
How to Submit Product Test Samples to CPRI:
1. Obtain a Test Request Form (TRF) or Manakonline Application Reference Number from BIS if applying under BIS Product Certification / CRS Scheme.
2. Fill out the CPRI Testing Requisition Form available on the CPRI customer portal (www.cpri.res.in), specifying the applicable Indian Standard (IS code) and test parameters required.
3. Securely pack product test samples with tamper-evident seals and attach official identification labels stating sample manufacturer, batch number, ratings, and BIS application ID.
4. Deliver or courier the sample to the CPRI Central Reception / Customer Service Cell along with the advance testing fee and manufacturer test certificate (MTC).
5. Following testing, CPRI issues an accredited test report and uploads it electronically to the BIS Manakonline portal for grant of license or CRS approval.

Protocol for Submitting Product Samples for BIS Conformity Testing:
1. Preliminary Application: The applicant must have a valid application registered on Manakonline (www.manakonline.in) for Scheme I (ISI Mark) or Scheme II (CRS).
2. Sample Drawing & Counter-Sealing: Under Normal Procedure, samples are drawn during factory audit by the BIS inspecting officer and counter-sealed. Under Simplified Procedure / Option 2, the manufacturer submits self-drawn samples directly to an LRS recognized lab before audit.
3. Documentation: Each sample consignment must include: (a) BIS Test Request Form (TRF), (b) Copy of Form I application, (c) Detailed technical construction file (TCF) / circuit diagram, (d) Payment receipt of prescribed testing charges.
4. Receipt & Witnessing: Lab acknowledges receipt on the portal. Manufacturer may request to witness non-destructive tests where permissible under standard guidelines.

[BIS Certification Schemes Matrix] BIS Product Certification Schemes — Comprehensive Overview
Scheme I — ISI Mark:
BIS Product Certification Scheme I (ISI Mark): For domestic Indian manufacturers.
- Purpose: Certifies that a product conforms to the relevant Indian Standard.
- Process: Application → Factory inspection by BIS officers → Product sample testing in BIS-recognized lab → License grant.
- License validity: 1 year initially, renewable annually.
- Fees: Application fee ₹1,000; Annual marking fee based on production volume (0.1% to 0.2% of ex-factory value, subject to minimum/maximum caps).
- Surveillance: BIS conducts periodic surprise inspections and market sample testing.
- ISI mark components: ISI logo (triangle), IS standard number, CM/L (Certification Marks License) number.
- Products: Covers cement, steel, food items, electrical appliances, helmets, cylinders, pressure cookers, water purifiers, and 500+ other product categories.
title: BIS Product Certification Schemes — Comprehensive Overview

metadata.title: BIS Product Certification Schemes — Comprehensive Overview

text:
[BIS Certification Schemes Matrix] BIS Product Certification Schemes — Comprehensive Overview
Scheme II — CRS:
BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS / Scheme II): For electronics and IT goods.
- Purpose: Ensures safety of electronic and IT products sold in India.
- Applicable to: Products notified under the Electronics and Information Technology Goods (Requirements for Compulsory Registration) Order by MeitY.
- Key product categories: LED lamps, LED luminaires, UPS systems, power banks, adapters, fixed/portable computers, printers, monitors, set-top boxes, smart watches.
- Process: Manufacturer/importer gets products tested at BIS-recognized lab → Submits test report + application on BIS portal (manakonline.bis.gov.in) → BIS issues Registration Certificate.
- Key difference from ISI: No factory inspection required — it's self-declaration based after lab testing.
- Registration validity: 2 years, renewable.
- Fee: Registration fee ₹1,000 per model per standard.
- Foreign manufacturers: Must appoint an Authorized Indian Representative (AIR) who takes legal responsibility.
title: BIS Product Certification Schemes — Comprehensive Overview

metadata.title: BIS Product Certification Schemes — Comprehensive Overview

text:
[BIS Certification Schemes Matrix] BIS Product Certification Schemes — Comprehensive Overview
FMCS:
FMCS (Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme): For overseas manufacturers exporting to India.
- Purpose: Enables foreign manufacturers to obtain ISI mark certification for products exported to India.
- Requirements:
  1. Appoint an Authorized Indian Representative (AIR) resident in India.
  2. Application through AIR on BIS portal.
  3. Factory inspection by BIS officers at the foreign manufacturing facility (manufacturer bears travel and inspection costs).
  4. Product testing at a BIS-recognized lab.
  5. License grant upon compliance.
- Fees: Same as Scheme I, plus travel costs for BIS officers.
- Validity: Same as Scheme I (1 year, renewable).
- The AIR is legally responsible for the product's conformity in India.

[BIS Certification Schemes Matrix] BIS Product Certification Schemes — Comprehensive Overview
Scheme X:
BIS Scheme X: Certification against non-Indian standards.
- Purpose: Allows manufacturers to get BIS certification for products conforming to international standards (ISO, IEC, ASTM, etc.) when no equivalent Indian Standard exists.
- Process: Similar to Scheme I, but assessment is done against the specified international/foreign standard.
- Use case: Products for export or products where an Indian Standard hasn't been published yet.
- Less commonly used than Schemes I and II.

ECO Mark:
BIS ECO Mark Scheme: Voluntary environmental certification.
- Purpose: Certifies that products meet specific environmental criteria in addition to quality requirements.
- Applicable product categories: Soaps and detergents, paper/paper products, food items, lubricating oils, packaging materials, paints/varnishes, batteries, electrical/electronic goods, textiles, cosmetics, plastics, fire extinguishers.
- Process: Product must first conform to the relevant Indian Standard + meet additional ECO Mark criteria (biodegradability, minimal toxicity, energy efficiency, recyclability).
- The ECO Mark logo is an earthen pot (matka) symbol.
- Voluntary scheme — not mandatory, but increasingly valued by environmentally-conscious consumers.

[BIS Consumer Guide] Consumer Rights, Verification & Grievance Mechanisms
1.0 Consumer Complaint Channels:
How consumers can file complaints about substandard or counterfeit ISI-marked products:
1. BIS Care App: Available on Android (Google Play) and iOS (App Store). Scan the ISI mark or enter the license number to report a complaint directly.
2. BIS Website: Online complaint form at www.bis.gov.in → 'Consumer Corner' → 'File a Complaint'.
3. Email: Send complaint details to ccd@bis.gov.in (Consumer Complaints Division).
4. Toll-free Helpline: 1800-11-4100 (available Monday–Friday, 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM IST).
5. Written Complaint: Send by post to the nearest BIS Regional/Branch Office.

Required information for complaints: Product details, ISI mark number, CM/L number, date of purchase, seller details, nature of complaint, and photographic evidence if possible.

text:
[BIS Consumer Guide] Consumer Rights, Verification & Grievance Mechanisms
2.0 ISI Mark Verification:
How to verify if an ISI mark is genuine:
A genuine ISI mark consists of:
1. The ISI logo (a triangular figure with 'ISI' text inside)
2. The IS standard number (e.g., IS 2347 for pressure cookers)
3. A CM/L (Certification Marks License) number unique to the manufacturer

Verification methods:
1. BIS Care App: Enter the CM/L number to verify the manufacturer's license status.
2. BIS Website: Visit www.bis.gov.in → 'Know Your Standards' → 'Verify License'.
3. Check the CM/L number format: It follows the pattern 'CM/L-XXXXXXX' where X are digits.

Warning signs of fake ISI marks:
- Blurry or poorly printed ISI logo
- Missing CM/L number
- CM/L number that returns 'no record found' on BIS portal
- ISI mark without the IS standard number
- Products from categories where ISI mark is mandatory but mark looks suspicious

text:
[BIS Consumer Guide] Consumer Rights, Verification & Grievance Mechanisms
3.0 Penalties for Misuse:
Penalties under BIS Act 2016 for misuse:
1. Using ISI mark without license: Fine of ₹2 lakh to ₹5 lakh, imprisonment up to 2 years, or both.
2. Using counterfeit ISI mark: Fine up to ₹10 lakh and imprisonment up to 2 years.
3. Selling non-conforming products with ISI mark: Fine of minimum ₹1 lakh or 10 times the value of goods (whichever is more).
4. Selling without mandatory BIS certification (for compulsory items): Fine of ₹2 lakh + ₹2 lakh for each subsequent offence.
5. Obstructing BIS officers during inspection: Fine up to ₹1 lakh.

BIS has the power to:
- Suspend or cancel licenses
- Order product recall
- File criminal complaints
- Seize non-conforming goods
- Publish names of non-compliant manufacturers

[BIS Hallmarking Order 2020] Bureau of Indian Standards (Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery and Gold Artefacts) Order, 2020
3.0 Mandatory Hallmarking:
Mandatory hallmarking implementation phases:
- Phase 1 (June 16, 2021): Mandatory hallmarking enforced in 256 districts across India.
- Phase 2 (June 2022): Extended to additional districts.
- Phase 3 (April 2023): Mandatory hallmarking now applicable in ALL districts of India.

Who must comply: All jewellers selling gold jewellery/artefacts must register with BIS and sell only hallmarked gold jewellery.
Penalties for non-compliance:
- First offence: Fine up to ₹1 lakh
- Subsequent offences: Fine up to ₹5 lakh and/or imprisonment up to 1 year
- Selling jewellery below declared purity: Action under BIS Act 2016 — fine up to 10 times the value of goods or ₹1 lakh minimum

Stage 3 — Sample Testing:
Stage 3: Product Sample Testing
1. Samples are drawn by BIS officers during the factory visit.
2. Samples are sent to a BIS-recognized laboratory for testing against the relevant IS standard.
3. Test reports are typically available within 15-30 days.
4. Testing fees are borne by the manufacturer and vary by product complexity.

[BIS Licensing Process Guide] BIS 5-Stage Licensing Process & Fee Structure for MSMEs & Startups
Stage 4 — License Grant:
Stage 4: License Grant
1. If factory assessment and sample testing are satisfactory, BIS grants the license.
2. The manufacturer receives a unique CM/L (Certification Marks License) number.
3. The license authorizes use of the ISI mark on conforming products.
4. License validity: 1 year from date of grant.
5. The CM/L number must be displayed alongside the ISI mark on every product.
6. Total time from application to license: typically 60-90 days.

text:
[BIS Licensing Process Guide] BIS 5-Stage Licensing Process & Fee Structure for MSMEs & Startups
Stage 5 — Surveillance:
Stage 5: Surveillance & Renewal
1. BIS conducts surprise surveillance visits (at least once per year).
2. Market samples may be purchased and tested for conformity.
3. Annual renewal: Submit renewal application + pay marking fee before license expiry.
4. Marking fee: 0.1% to 0.2% of ex-factory value of ISI-marked production, subject to minimum ₹1,000 and maximum cap.
5. MSMEs and startups get special fee concessions — reduced marking fees and expedited processing.
6. Non-renewal or non-compliance: License suspension or cancellation. Continued use of ISI mark after cancellation is a criminal offence.

[BIS Overview] Bureau of Indian Standards — About BIS
1.0 About BIS:
Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is the national standards body of India established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. It functions under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution. BIS is responsible for:
1. Formulating Indian Standards (IS codes) — over 22,000 standards published covering food, electronics, construction, chemicals, textiles, automotive, and more.
2. Product certification (ISI mark under Scheme I, CRS under Scheme II, FMCS for foreign manufacturers).
3. Hallmarking of precious metals (gold, silver).
4. Laboratory recognition and testing.
5. Consumer protection related to standardized products.
6. Promoting quality consciousness through Standards Clubs.

BIS has its headquarters in New Delhi with 5 Regional Offices (Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Chandigarh) and 36 Branch Offices across India.
Website: www.bis.gov.in | Helpline: 1800-11-4100
title: Bureau of Indian Standards — About BIS

text:
[BIS Overview] Bureau of Indian Standards — About BIS
2.0 BIS Act 2016:
Key provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016:
- Replaced the old Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986.
- Empowers the Central Government to notify products for mandatory certification.
- Provides for compulsory hallmarking of precious metals.
- Stricter penalties for misuse of Standard Mark (ISI mark) — up to ₹10 lakh fine and 2 years imprisonment.
- Enables BIS to establish labs and recognize external laboratories.
- Provides for recall of non-conforming products.
- Enables online registration and licensing through manakonline.bis.gov.in portal.
- Special provisions for MSMEs and startups with reduced fees and faster processing.

[IS 10500:2012] Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)
1.0 Scope:
This standard prescribes the quality requirements and methods of sampling and test for drinking water (piped water supplies, packaged drinking water, water from public wells, borewells, and tankers). It sets limits for physical, chemical, and bacteriological parameters to ensure the water is wholesome and safe for domestic human consumption.
title: Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)

metadata.title: Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)

text:
[IS 10500:2012] Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)
Table 1 — Physical & Organoleptic Parameters:
Requirements for physical characteristics of drinking water:
- Colour: Acceptable limit 5 Hazen units max; Permissible limit in the absence of alternate source is 15 Hazen units max.
- Odour: Agreeable.
- Taste: Agreeable.
- Turbidity: Acceptable limit 1 NTU max; Permissible limit in the absence of alternate source is 5 NTU max.
- pH Value: Acceptable range 6.5 to 8.5; No relaxation.
- Total Dissolved Solids (TDS): Acceptable limit 500 mg/L max; Permissible limit in the absence of alternate source is 2000 mg/L max.
title: Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)

metadata.title: Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)

text:
[IS 10500:2012] Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)
Table 2 — Chemical Parameters:
Key chemical parameters and limits:
- Iron (Fe): Acceptable 0.3 mg/L; Permissible 1.0 mg/L (causes staining and taste issues above limits)
- Fluoride: Acceptable 1.0 mg/L; Permissible 1.5 mg/L (excess causes dental/skeletal fluorosis)
- Arsenic: Acceptable 0.01 mg/L; Permissible 0.05 mg/L (toxic heavy metal)
- Lead: Acceptable 0.01 mg/L; No relaxation (neurotoxic)
- Nitrate (as NO3): Acceptable 45 mg/L; No relaxation (causes methemoglobinemia in infants)
- Total Hardness (as CaCO3): Acceptable 200 mg/L; Permissible 600 mg/L
- Chloride: Acceptable 250 mg/L; Permissible 1000 mg/L
- Residual Free Chlorine: Minimum 0.2 mg/L at consumer end for disinfection
title: Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)

metadata.title: Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)

text:
[IS 10500:2012] Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)
Table 3 — Bacteriological Parameters:
Bacteriological requirements for drinking water:
- E. coli or Thermotolerant Coliform: Shall not be detectable in any 100 mL sample.
- Total Coliform: Shall not be detectable in any 100 mL sample (piped treated supply).
- All drinking water samples should be free from pathogenic organisms.
Testing method: IS 1622 (Methods of sampling and microbiological examination of water).

Table 1 — Fineness Grades:
Permitted gold fineness grades as per IS 1417 (for hallmarking):
- 14 carat (14K): Minimum fineness 585 parts per thousand (58.5% pure gold)
- 18 carat (18K): Minimum fineness 750 parts per thousand (75% pure gold)
- 20 carat (20K): Minimum fineness 833 parts per thousand (83.3% pure gold)

text:
[IS 1417:2016] Gold and Gold Alloys — Jewellery/Artefacts — Fineness and Marking — Specification
5.0 Hallmarking Procedure:
Hallmarking procedure for gold jewellery:
1. Jeweller submits articles to a BIS-recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centre (AHC).
2. AHC assays (tests) the gold purity using fire assay or XRF method.
3. If purity conforms to declared caratage, the article receives:
   - BIS Standard Mark (triangle logo)
   - Purity grade mark (e.g., '916' for 22K)
   - HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) — a 6-character alphanumeric code
4. HUID is laser-engraved or stamped on the article.
5. HUID data is uploaded to BIS central server and is publicly verifiable.

As of Phase 3 (April 2023), mandatory hallmarking applies in ALL districts across India.
Exemptions: Export jewellery, watches, fountain pens, and special-order items above 10 grams.
title: Gold and Gold Alloys — Jewellery/Artefacts — Fineness and Marking — Specification

metadata.title: Gold and Gold Alloys — Jewellery/Artefacts — Fineness and Marking — Specification

text:
[IS 1417:2016] Gold and Gold Alloys — Jewellery/Artefacts — Fineness and Marking — Specification
6.0 HUID Verification:
How consumers can verify hallmarked gold jewellery:
1. BIS Care App: Available on Android (Google Play) and iOS (App Store). Scan or enter the 6-character HUID.
2. BIS Website: Visit www.bis.gov.in → Verify HUID → Enter the code.
3. SMS: Send 'VERIFY <HUID>' to the BIS helpline number.

HUID verification shows:
- Jeweller name and registration number
- Purity grade (e.g., 22K 916)
- AHC (Assaying & Hallmarking Centre) that certified the article
- Date of hallmarking

If verification fails or shows different purity than declared, consumers can file a complaint with BIS.

Key safety tests for toys under IS 9873:

- Sharp edge test: No accessible sharp edges before or after abuse testing
